name: Liechtenstein
summary: Liechtenstein taxes wealth instead of investment income. Net wealth (excluding foreign real estate) is converted into a deemed income of 4% (Sollertrag, Art. 5 SteG) and taxed with other income at the progressive state rate (top 8%) plus a municipal surcharge of 150%-250% of the state tax (Art. 75); Vaduz and Schaan kept 150% for 2025, which makes the wealth tax up to 0.8% a year (0.896% at 180%). In return, dividends, interest and gains on shares and other movable private assets are exempt from income tax. There is no inheritance or gift tax. Liechtenstein real estate gains bear a separate tax of up to 24%. Two alternatives are modelled: lump-sum taxation on expenditure (25% of living costs, government minimum CHF 300,000 a year, worse than the ordinary tax below roughly CHF 40 million of wealth) and a private foundation with proxy taxation, which pays about the same wealth tax and brings succession and asset-protection benefits, not a saving. The main obstacle is residence: permits for EEA nationals are limited by quota and partly by lottery, and very limited for others.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (wealth and income tax)
regimes.description: Combined wealth and income tax (Vermögens- und Erwerbssteuer) under the Tax Act (SteG, LGBl. 2010.340). Wealth is taxed through a 4% deemed return added to taxable income; actual returns on that wealth are exempt.
regimes.eligibility: Domicile (intention to stay permanently) or habitual residence of more than six months in Liechtenstein. Requires a residence permit, which is the main practical barrier.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on movable and immovable private assets are exempt from income tax (Art. 15(2)(m) SteG), as are gains on shares (Art. 15(2)(o)) and gains on foreign real estate (Art. 15(2)(l)). Gains on Liechtenstein real estate are taxed separately by the real estate gains tax: the income tax tariff for single persons (top 8%) plus a fixed 200% surcharge, up to 24%. Capital losses are not deductible.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: All private capital gains on movable assets exempt. Real estate gains tax: the basic allowance of the single-person tariff (CHF 15,855) applies.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Assets held as private assets. Business assets follow different rules (anti-abuse rules for passive low-taxed foreign participations).
capital_gains.regional_differences: Municipal surcharge differs by municipality but does not affect exempt gains; the real estate gains surcharge is a fixed 200%.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Business-asset participations in passive, low-taxed foreign entities can lose the exemption. Indirect transfers of real estate companies trigger real estate gains tax.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Movable assets, shares and foreign real estate: exempt under Art. 15(2)(l), (m), (o) SteG. Liechtenstein real estate: Art. 42 applies the Art. 19(1)(a) tariff (top marginal 8% from CHF 211,401) and Art. 43 adds a 200% surcharge instead of the municipal surcharge: 8% x 3 = 24%. Headline = that 24%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Professional securities dealing would be business income (taxed via the income tax), but the private-asset exemption is broad; no recharacterisation guidance was found.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign securities: same exemption. Foreign real estate: excluded from wealth tax (Art. 10(e)) and its gains exempt (Art. 15(2)(l)), with progression reservation for the rate (Art. 21).

dividends.summary: Dividends and profit shares from participations in legal entities are exempt from income tax for private shareholders (Art. 15(2)(n) SteG), as are all returns on wealth subject to wealth tax (Art. 15(1)(a)). The wealth tax (deemed return) replaces dividend tax.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign withholding tax on dividends cannot be credited because no Liechtenstein tax arises on them; treaty reduction at source is the only relief.
open_questions: Size of Liechtenstein's treaty network and whether foreign withholding can be reduced for residents was not verified (Liechtenstein has a limited network, including Switzerland, Austria, Germany, the UK and Luxembourg, from general knowledge).
dividends.rate_basis: Art. 15(2)(n) SteG exempts profit shares; Art. 15(1)(a) exempts returns on wealth subject to wealth tax. Rate 0.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Liechtenstein abolished its dividend coupon tax in 2011 (from general knowledge; PwC's withholding section not opened); companies distribute without withholding.
dividends.treaty_network: Small treaty network; not verified in this session.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 12.5% profit tax (Art. 61) with a CHF 1,800 minimum tax (Art. 62); private asset structures (PVS, Art. 64) pay only the minimum tax and are not assessed. A resident founder has two ways to use an irrevocable foundation: (a) apply for proxy taxation (Art. 9(3) SteG), so that the foundation pays the beneficiaries' wealth tax on the 4% deemed return at the single-person tariff (Art. 19(2)) and distributions to the beneficiaries are tax-free (Art. 14(2)(k)); no dedication tax arises (Art. 13(1) applies only when no application was filed); this is modelled as the stiftung_pvs regime; or (b) no application: 3.5% dedication tax plus the municipal surcharge once (8.75% at 150%), and distributions are taxable income. A revocable foundation is attributed to the founder (Art. 9(4)). The saving of proxy taxation over holding personally is nil (same 0.8% top rate, but no joint basic allowance); the reasons to use it are succession and asset protection.

wealth_tax.summary: Wealth tax is levied through the income tax: worldwide net wealth (excluding foreign real estate and foreign permanent establishments) is multiplied by a 4% standard return (Sollertrag, Art. 5 SteG; Art. 14(2)(l)) and taxed together with other income at the progressive state tariff (Art. 19; marginal 1%-8%), plus a municipal surcharge set each year by the municipality between 150% and 250% of the state tax (Art. 75(3)). The surcharge is 150% in Vaduz and Schaan (2025; the 2026 figure was not found). For a married couple whose only income is the deemed return, the effective marginal wealth tax rises to 0.8% at 150% (0.896% at 180%).
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Household goods and private cars up to CHF 52,800 for a married couple; foreign real estate exempt. The income tax basic allowance (CHF 31,710 joint) makes the first ~CHF 792,750 of wealth tax-free if there is no other income.
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: All residents taxed in the ordinary way.
wealth_tax.regional_differences: The municipal surcharge varies (legal range 150%-250%); the brackets assume 150%.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Because the deemed return is added to other income, earned or pension income pushes the deemed return into higher bands sooner. Transfers into a structure that leaves the wealth tax base bear a one-off 3.5% dedication tax (Art. 13) plus the municipal surcharge, unless the structure applies for proxy taxation (Art. 9(3), see the stiftung_pvs regime). The tariff is not indexed automatically: Art. 20 SteG adjusts tariff and amounts only if consumer prices have risen 3% or more since the last adjustment and the Landtag agrees on the government's motion, so thresholds_indexed stays false. Lump-sum taxation on expenditure (Art. 30-34) replaces wealth and income tax for qualifying newcomers (see the lump_sum regime).

Gemeinde Schaan: oeffentliches Protokoll, Sitzung vom 26. November 2025 (Gemeindesteuerzuschlag Steuerjahr 2025 definitiv 150 %)
Liechtenstein - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: The 2026 municipal surcharge for Vaduz and Schaan was not found; 2025 was 150% in both (council protocols). Brackets assume the statutory minimum 150%; scale rates by (1+surcharge)/2.5 for other municipalities (WeTrust names 160% in Eschen and Mauren as the highest at present).

Brackets assume no income besides the deemed return and joint assessment of a married couple (Art. 19(1)(c) tariff); child and insurance deductions (Art. 16(3): CHF 12,700 per child, up to CHF 7,400 + 2,200 per child) are ignored.

components.name: Wealth tax via 4% deemed return (Vermögenssteuer als Sollertrag)
components.notes: Derived from Art. 19(1)(c) SteG (married couples): marginal state rates 0/1/3/4/5/6/6.5/7/8% with income thresholds CHF 31,710 / 42,280 / 84,560 / 147,980 / 211,400 / 274,820 / 338,240 / 422,800 (the statute's formula 'rate x income - constant' equals the sum of these bands to within CHF 0.5). Wealth thresholds = income thresholds / 0.04 (Art. 5). Effective wealth rate = 4% x state rate x 2.5 (150% municipal surcharge, Art. 75(3)). Base excludes foreign real estate (Art. 10(e)).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No separate property tax; Liechtenstein real estate is part of the wealth tax base.

inheritance.summary: Liechtenstein levies no inheritance, estate or gift tax. Inheritances and gifts are also exempt from income tax (Art. 15(2)(c) SteG). The heirs simply include the assets in their own wealth tax base afterwards.
inheritance.important_exceptions: A 3.5% dedication tax (Widmungssteuer, Art. 13 SteG) plus the municipal surcharge (Art. 75(1)) applies when assets are transferred to a legal entity or foundation so that they leave the wealth tax base, the interests cannot be valued and no application for proxy taxation (Art. 9(3)) was filed; not relevant to direct gifts to children. Inheritances and gifts received are income-tax free (Art. 15(2)(c)).
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax; gifts are exempt from income tax. Only the dedication tax applies to transfers into structures outside the wealth tax base.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on any assets; foreign estate taxes of situs countries may apply.

regimes.name: Lump-sum taxation on expenditure (Besteuerung nach dem Aufwand)
regimes.description: On application, newcomers who do not work in Liechtenstein and live on foreign income or assets pay 25% of their total worldwide living costs (government minimum CHF 300,000 a year) instead of wealth and income tax (Art. 30-34 SteG). Dividends, gains and foreign wealth are covered; Liechtenstein real estate stays under ordinary wealth tax. It beats the ordinary tax only for wealth above roughly CHF 38-40 million (WeTrust).
regimes.eligibility: Non-Liechtenstein citizens (a dual citizen with Liechtenstein nationality does not qualify) who take up domicile or habitual residence for the first time or after at least ten years abroad, do not work in Liechtenstein and live on income or assets from abroad (Art. 30(1) SteG). There is no right to the regime: the Steuerverwaltung decides on application (Art. 31). A residence permit is needed first (EEA quota and lottery, see residency).
regimes.duration_note: No statutory time limit (Art. 30-34 SteG). In practice the tax is fixed for five years and renews by one year unless either side asks for a new assessment (WeTrust). It ends with deregistration, a request for ordinary taxation or the death of one spouse; the survivor then falls under ordinary tax unless the lump sum is applied for again (WeTrust).

lump_sum.notes: Tax = 25% of total annual expenditure of the family worldwide (Art. 32-33 SteG), but at least CHF 300,000 a year: the government has set a minimum tax of CHF 300,000, i.e. living costs of CHF 1.2 million at 25% (WeTrust, updated 3 Aug 2026; the minimum is not in the SteG or the SteV, which were both read). The reference family spends EUR 400,000 a year, so 25% of its costs (about CHF 90,000-100,000) is below the minimum and the minimum applies: CHF 300,000 a year. The tax replaces wealth tax and income tax on everything except Liechtenstein real estate, which stays under ordinary wealth tax with no debt deduction (Art. 30(3)); the family's CHF 5M-equivalent home is therefore taxed on top and is not in the amount. Whether the municipal surcharge is included in the CHF 300,000 was not found (the adviser's break-even of about CHF 39.5 million of wealth at a 150% surcharge suggests it is the all-in figure). Not indexed by law: the minimum is a government decision.

capital_gains.summary: Covered by the lump sum, as in the ordinary regime private gains on movable assets and on foreign real estate are in any case exempt (Art. 15(2)(l), (m), (o)). Liechtenstein real estate gains bear the real estate gains tax outside the lump sum.

sources.title: Die Pauschalbesteuerung in Liechtenstein - ein Ueberblick (WeTrust, updated 3 Aug 2026)

capital_gains.rate_basis: Same as the standard regime: exempt except Liechtenstein real estate (Art. 42-43 SteG, 8% x 3 = 24%); the lump sum does not change gains tax on Liechtenstein property (WeTrust: Grundstueckgewinnsteuer not covered).

dividends.summary: Dividends are covered by the lump sum and in any case exempt for private shareholders (Art. 15(1)(a), 15(2)(n) SteG). No Liechtenstein tax can be credited against foreign withholding. A lump-sum taxpayer cannot claim a credit for foreign tax (Art. 18a(3)(a) SteV); WeTrust says lump-sum taxpayers are treated as Liechtenstein residents and can use the treaty network.

sources.title: Die Pauschalbesteuerung in Liechtenstein - ein Ueberblick (WeTrust, updated 3 Aug 2026)

open_questions: Whether treaty relief at source (15% instead of the statutory rate) is available to lump-sum taxpayers rests on WeTrust (yes); a search result mentioned an Austrian ministry ruling (EAS 3449) denying it for the Austria treaty, which was not opened; not resolved.
dividends.rate_basis: Covered by the lump sum; 0 on top of it.

wealth_tax.summary: No separate wealth tax: the lump sum replaces wealth and income tax (Art. 30(1) SteG), except on Liechtenstein real estate, which stays under ordinary wealth tax without debt deduction (Art. 30(3)).

sources.title: Die Pauschalbesteuerung in Liechtenstein - ein Ueberblick (WeTrust, updated 3 Aug 2026)

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Liechtenstein real estate remains subject to ordinary wealth tax (deemed return at the ordinary tariff) with no allowances or debt deduction (Art. 30(3) SteG); it is not in the lump sum amount.

sources.title: Die Pauschalbesteuerung in Liechtenstein - ein Ueberblick (WeTrust, updated 3 Aug 2026)

regimes.name: Liechtenstein private foundation (Stiftung) with PVS status and proxy taxation
regimes.description: The family endows an irrevocable Liechtenstein foundation (PGR art. 552) with the portfolio. As a private asset structure (PVS, Art. 64 SteG) it pays only the CHF 1,800 minimum profit tax and is not assessed. The family applies for proxy taxation (Art. 9(3) SteG): the foundation pays the beneficiaries' wealth tax on a 4% deemed return, so no dedication tax arises (Art. 13) and distributions to the beneficiaries are tax-free (Art. 14(2)(k)). The wealth tax is about the same as holding personally (0.8% at the top). The reasons to use the structure are succession planning, asset protection and continuity; nothing is saved in tax. Inheritance tax does not exist either way, so the standard inheritance rules are inherited.
regimes.eligibility: Any resident can found a Liechtenstein foundation: minimum capital CHF 30,000 (Grant Thornton), at least two members of the foundation council, one of them a domestic fiduciary or equivalent (Grant Thornton). PVS status needs a purpose limited to financial instruments, participations, cash and bank balances, no economic activity, investors who are private persons or private structures, and annual confirmations to the Steuerverwaltung (Art. 64(1)-(4) SteG). If the founder keeps control, the foundation can be treated as a controlled (sham) foundation, and a revocable one is attributed to the founder (Art. 9(4)).
regimes.duration_note: A foundation has no statutory time limit; PVS status is confirmed every year (Art. 64(4) SteG).

structure.entity: Stiftung (PGR art. 552 ff.) with PVS status (Art. 64 SteG)
structure.payout_notes: Distributions to resident beneficiaries are not taxable income when the foundation has applied for proxy taxation, because the entitlement then bears wealth tax in the foundation's hands (Art. 14(2)(k) SteG: benefits are income only 'soweit die Beguenstigung nicht ... Art. 9 Abs. 3 der Vermoegenssteuer unterliegt'). Without the application distributions are taxable income at the ordinary progressive rates (up to 8% x 2.5 = 20% at a 150% surcharge). The foundation's payments to beneficiaries are not deductible expenses (Art. 21(4) SteV: they are not 'Aufwand').
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: PVS conditions in Art. 64 SteG: no economic activity, only financial instruments, participations, cash and bank balances; shares not publicly placed; statutes must state the PVS restrictions; no control over participations held; annual confirmation and accounting under PGR art. 1045 ff. The running cost recorded is the statutory minimum tax of CHF 1,800 (Art. 62(2)); fees of the domestic fiduciary on the foundation council, administration, audit and legal advice are not included because no sourced figure was found. A one-off formation duty of 2 per mille of the capital, minimum CHF 200, applies on formation (Art. 66(3)); whether it also applies to later endowments (CHF 60,000 on a CHF 30 million endowment) was not confirmed and is not counted.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Revocation or change of the arrangements so that the beneficiaries' interests leave the wealth tax base can trigger Art. 13(2) (3.5% plus surcharge). The foundation is a separate person; the founders' later emigration does not move its assets. Foundation distributions to non-residents were not researched.

capital_gains.summary: A private asset structure (PVS) pays only the CHF 1,800 minimum tax and is not assessed (Art. 64(8) SteG); gains on shares and other participations are exempt for legal persons in any case (Art. 48(1)(f)). Gains on Liechtenstein real estate bear the real estate gains tax (24%, Art. 42-43), which a PVS holding financial instruments would not have.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Art. 64(8) SteG: a PVS is subject only to the minimum tax (Art. 62(1)-(2)) and is not assessed; Art. 48(1)(e)-(f): profit shares and gains on participations are exempt from profit tax anyway. Liechtenstein real estate: Art. 42-43, 24%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Same treatment for foreign financial instruments.

dividends.summary: Dividends and distributions received by a PVS are not taxed (Art. 64(8) SteG: minimum tax only; Art. 48(1)(e)). Foreign withholding tax cannot be credited and is a final cost; a PVS pays only CHF 1,800 of Liechtenstein tax, so treaty relief at source may be refused (not verified).
open_questions: Whether a PVS obtains treaty-reduced source withholding was not verified; if it does not, the statutory withholding of each source country applies.
dividends.rate_basis: 0% at foundation level: Art. 64(8) SteG leaves only the minimum tax.
dividends.holding_company_notes: This is the foundation itself; the wealth tax it pays in place of its beneficiaries is in wealth_tax, and distributions are tax-free for the beneficiaries (Art. 14(2)(k)).

wealth_tax.summary: On application (Art. 9(3) SteG) the irrevocable foundation pays the beneficiaries' wealth tax in their place: the 4% deemed return of the foundation's assets (Art. 5) is taxed at the single-person tariff of Art. 19(1)(a) with no basic allowance and each deduction reduced by CHF 159 (Art. 19(2)), plus the municipal surcharge (150% in Vaduz and Schaan in 2025; assumed to apply, Art. 75(1)). At the top this is 0.8% of wealth, the same as for the couple holding personally, but without the couple's joint allowance (about CHF 16,500 a year more at the top rate).
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: Irrevocable foundation, application by a beneficiary with the consent of the body deciding on distributions (Art. 9(3)); to be filed by 31 December of the tax year (Art. 7 SteV). The foundation's assets must be those of a private asset structure (Art. 64) for the minimum-tax treatment.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: A revocable foundation is attributed to the founder and taxed at the founder's own rate (Art. 9(4)). Without an application, the transfer attracts the 3.5% dedication tax (Art. 13) and distributions are taxable income (Art. 14(2)(k)). Whether the municipal surcharge applies to proxy taxation was not found stated; Art. 75(1) levies it on the Vermoegens- und Erwerbssteuer of unlimited taxpayers, which the foundation is (Art. 44).

sources.title: Gemeinde Vaduz: oeffentliches Protokoll der 27. Sitzung des Gemeinderates vom 5. November 2024 (Gemeindesteuerzuschlag 2025 bei 150 % belassen)

open_questions: Whether the municipal surcharge (Art. 75) is levied on tax paid by the foundation under Art. 9(3), and at which municipality's rate (the seat's), was not found stated; the brackets assume 150%. Without the surcharge the tax would be 40% lower.

components.name: Proxy wealth tax of the foundation on the 4% deemed return (Art. 9(3), 19(2) SteG)
components.notes: Art. 19(1)(a) tariff on the deemed return: bands to CHF 21,140 / 42,280 / 73,990 / 105,700 / 137,410 / 169,120 / 211,400 at 1/3/4/5/6/6.5/7% and 8% above, with no basic allowance (Art. 19(2): 'Grundfreibetrag nicht zu beruecksichtigen', so the first band 1% starts at zero). Wealth thresholds = deemed-return thresholds / 0.04. Effective wealth rate = 4% x state rate x 2.5 (150% surcharge). Equals 'tax = 0.08 x return - 6,289' above CHF 211,400 (6,448 less 159).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Liechtenstein real estate held by the foundation is part of its wealth tax base.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident with a domicile in Liechtenstein (living there with the intention to stay) or a habitual residence of more than six months.

routes.name: EEA nationals: residence permit within a quota (partly by lottery)
routes.requirements: Liechtenstein is in the EEA but restricts free movement: the government may set maximum numbers of permits (Art. 10 PFZG) and in practice allocates part of the annual quota by lottery (reported figures for non-working persons are small, press reports of about 8 permits a year; not verified, the official apa.llv.li pages were not reached). A permit without gainful activity requires enough means not to need social assistance and comprehensive health insurance (Art. 22 PFZG). Lump-sum taxation is open to such permit holders (Art. 30 SteG).

routes.name: Third-country nationals
routes.requirements: Permits under the Foreigners Act are granted only exceptionally and the government decides (WeTrust: persons without gainful activity need sufficient means). No investor or golden-visa programme known. Not verified against the Migration and Passport Office.

sources.title: Die Pauschalbesteuerung in Liechtenstein - ein Ueberblick (WeTrust, updated 3 Aug 2026)

corporate.summary: Flat 12.5% profit tax on worldwide income; CHF 1,800 annual minimum tax (creditable), waived for small operating companies. Dividends and capital gains on participations generally exempt. Pillar Two 15% top-up for large groups. Private asset structures (PVS) pay only the minimum tax.

sources.title: Liechtenstein - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

cost_of_living.notes: Prime rent is a national median of ordinary family houses (no priced Vaduz listing). Second portal: nemo.li house rentals, https://nemo.li/mieten/art-haus/ ; Engel & Völkers Liechtenstein houses for rent: https://www.engelvoelkers.com/li/en/properties/res/rent/house . Price per m², health insurance and staff costs were not sourced.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: International School Rheintal (Buchs SG, Switzerland, about 5 km from Vaduz across the Rhine; IB Diploma), Grades 11-12 annual tuition 2026/2027 (Grades 6-10 CHF 31,880). One-time capital fund fee CHF 5,600 for the first child (CHF 4,100 second, CHF 2,600 third). Liechtenstein itself has no English-language international secondary school.

source.title: International School Rheintal: Financial Regulations 2026/2027 (schedule of fees)

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median of the ten priced houses of 5.5 rooms or more (Swiss room count; about 4+ bedrooms) offered to let across Liechtenstein on 15 Oct 2026 on the two Liechtenstein portals, immoboerse.li (ITW, all 13 house rentals in the country) and nemo.li (14 house rentals), duplicates removed: Schaan 6.5 rooms 3,450; Mauren 6.5 rooms 3,350; Balzers 7.5-room terraced houses from 2,750; Gamprin-Bendern 5.5 rooms 2,690; Schellenberg 5.5 rooms 2,500; Nendeln 5.5 rooms 2,500; Schaan 7.5 rooms (older house) 2,500; Eschen 6.5 rooms 2,400; Ruggell 6.5 rooms 2,400; Balzers 6.5 rooms 1,900 (CHF a month, mostly net of utilities). Not prime: none of the priced houses is in Vaduz. Engel & Völkers' three Vaduz houses the same day were a 5.5-room detached house (price on request), a premium 5.5-room house in the villa quarter (let, price on request) and a 5.5-room Städtle house (let, CHF 2,950 total rent); a 7.5-room, 225 m² Schaan house was price on request. A prime Vaduz family house therefore likely rents above this median. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

source.title: immoboerse.li: Häuser zu mieten in Liechtenstein

us_citizen_notes: No US-Liechtenstein income tax treaty (a TIEA and FATCA IGA exist). Liechtenstein's wealth-based tax is not an income tax on specific items, so US foreign tax credits for it are doubtful; US citizens pay full US tax on gains and dividends.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: lump-sum taxation on expenditure (Art. 30-34 SteG) is 25% of the family's worldwide living costs, at least CHF 300,000 a year, and Liechtenstein real estate remains under ordinary wealth tax with no debt deduction (Art. 30(3)). The engine's lump sum is one fixed amount that replaces all wealth tax and has no residual tax on local real estate. For the reference family (EUR 400,000 of spending) the minimum binds, so the fixed amount is exact apart from the home.

The CHF 300,000 minimum tax is stated by two Liechtenstein advisers (WeTrust, updated 2026) as set by the government; it is not in the SteG or the SteV, and no official publication of it was found. It is decisive: without it 25% of EUR 400,000 would be about CHF 90,000-100,000. Whether the municipal surcharge is inside the CHF 300,000 is not stated.

Residence permit rules: Art. 10 and 22 PFZG were read, but the size of the quota and the lottery rules (Ausländer- und Passamt, EEA Joint Committee decision 191/1999) were not verified from an official page.
Municipal surcharge: 150% in Vaduz and Schaan for 2025 (council protocols); the 2026 figure was not found.

Private foundation: whether the municipal surcharge applies to proxy taxation (Art. 9(3)), whether a PVS gets treaty relief on foreign dividends, and the foundation's real running and formation costs (formation duty Art. 66(3); fiduciary fees) were not found.

Prime rent is the CHF 2,500 median of ten ordinary 5.5+-room houses across Liechtenstein (immoboerse.li, nemo.li, 15 Oct 2026); no priced Vaduz house was listed. A Vaduz/Schaan prime figure from an agency would make the rent more representative.
